facts.raw_span: 4 days of blurry vision and pain in her left eye
after undergoing a routine dental cleaning 1 week prior
no history of gingival disease or cavities
Visual acuity was 20/25 OD and 20/50 OS
Intraocular pressures were 15 mm Hg OD and 11 mm Hg OS
conjunctival hyperemia, faint keratic precipitates, 3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber
mild nuclear sclerosis, and a whitish focal granuloma at the 4-o'clock position at the pupillary margin
no evidence of vitritis, retinitis, or vasculitis
visual acuity declined to 20/100 OS, with development of hypopyon and increased fibrinous material emanating from the iris lesion
Gram stain revealed gram-positive cocci in chains and gram-positive rods in a branching pattern
Aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius
Blood and urine cultures, electrocardiogram and echocardiogram were unremarkable

concepts.why: The patient presented with declining visual acuity, hypopyon, and increased fibrinous material emanating from the iris lesion, which are consistent with endophthalmitis, an intraocular infection.
The aerobic culture revealed Streptococcus intermedius, which is a type of streptococcal bacteria that can cause endophthalmitis.

The patient presented with conjunctival hyperemia, faint keratic precipitates, and 3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber, which are consistent with iritis, an inflammatory condition of the eye.

The patient presented with conjunctival hyperemia, faint keratic precipitates, and 3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber, which are consistent with uveitis, an inflammatory condition of the eye.
The patient underwent a routine dental cleaning 1 week prior to presentation, which may have introduced bacteria into the eye, leading to post-surgical endophthalmitis.

rationales.F01: Blurry vision and pain are common symptoms of endophthalmitis.
rationales.F02: Recent dental cleaning is a potential risk factor for endophthalmitis.
rationales.F06: Conjunctival hyperemia and keratic precipitates are signs of inflammation in the eye.
rationales.F09: Decline in visual acuity and development of hypopyon are indicative of severe intraocular inflammation.
rationales.F10: Gram-positive cocci in chains are consistent with Streptococcal infection.
rationales.F11: Aerobic culture revealing Streptococcus intermedius confirms the diagnosis of Streptococcal endophthalmitis.
